study_identification.title: Delineating the Heterogeneity of Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment Using Normative Models of Dynamic Brain Functional Networks

study_characteristics.study_objective: Construct sex-specific normative age models of dynamic functional connectivity (a-FCS, f-FCS) to quantify individual deviations and identify reproducible subtypes of AD and MCI; compare subtype differences in functional phenotypes, structural atrophy and cognitive trajectories.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Subtype comparisons on MMSE/MoCA; functional network deviation patterns (Yeo-17); regional GMV/CT differences (Brainnetome); longitudinal cognitive trajectory differences over 4-year follow-up in ADNI using linear regression with age/sex and months×subtype interaction.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Two reproducible AD and MCI subtypes emerged with opposite deviation patterns (positive vs negative) showing distinct functional phenotypes, structural atrophy, progression, and cognitive decline trajectories; negative-deviation MCI showed potential transformation toward AD with more severe decline.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using dFC-based normative deviations (a-FCS/f-FCS), clustering identified subtypes in AD and MCI. Positive-deviation subtypes (elevated FCS metrics) and negative-deviation subtypes (reduced FCS metrics) displayed markedly different intrinsic network patterns (e.g., DMN, DAN, limbic), corresponding GMV/CT differences, and distinct MMSE/MoCA profiles. Replication in ADNI confirmed subtype reproducibility; longitudinal analyses indicated subtype-specific cognitive decline rates and potential progression pathways from MCI to AD, particularly for negative-deviation profiles.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Harmonization across scanners/sites limited to per-site NC centering; no ComBat/HBR. Longitudinal data unavailable in the in-house dataset, and ADNI MCI longitudinal sample size was relatively small; modality differences may yield distinct subtypes across features.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Dynamic FC normative modeling offers individualized deviation mapping and stratifies AD/MCI into neurophysiological subtypes, supporting precision stratification; future work should incorporate robust multi-site harmonization and larger longitudinal cohorts.

general_notes.general_notes: Scanning protocols detailed in Table S2 (3T scanners across sites; EPI parameters vary). Per-site FD provided in Table S1. Brainnetome atlas and Yeo-17 networks used. Scripts available upon request; MATLAB 2019b/Python used.
